title: ort
excerpt: Safe, ergonomic Rust bindings for ONNX Runtime — run any ONNX model with GPU acceleration in production.
body_md:
# ort

ort provides safe Rust bindings to Microsoft's ONNX Runtime, the industry standard for high-performance ML inference.

## Key Features

- **Any model**: Run models from PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, etc.
- **GPU support**: CUDA, TensorRT, DirectML, CoreML
- **Safe API**: Rust's type system prevents common errors
- **Production-ready**: Used in production at scale

## Quick Start

```rust
let session = Session::builder()?
    .with_model_from_file("model.onnx")?;
```

title: Starflask
excerpt: Rust client library and CLI for the Starflask API — generate images, videos, 3D models, and more from the command line or your Rust code.
body_md:
# Starflask

Starflask is a Rust CLI and client library for the [Starflask](https://starflask.com) API. It lets you generate images, videos, 3D models, and process media — all from your terminal or Rust code.

## Install

```bash
cargo install starflask
```

## Why Starflask?

Starflask shines when used inside AI coding assistants like Claude Code. You can generate images on the fly without leaving your terminal — perfect for creating thumbnails, banners, and assets while building web apps.

![Using Starflask in Claude Code](/starflask_use.png)

## CLI Quick Start

```bash
# Store your API key
starflask auth set sk-your-key-here

# Generate an image
starflask jobs create image --payload '{"prompt": "a fox in a forest"}'

# Wait for it to finish
starflask jobs wait <job-id>

# Animate a still image
starflask animate ./photo.png --prompt "gentle waves" --duration 5 --wait
```

## Library Usage

```rust
use starflask::Client;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), starflask::Error> {
    let client = Client::new("sk-your-key");

    let job = client.create_job("image", Some(serde_json::json!({
        "prompt": "a fox in a forest"
    }))).await?;

    let result = client.wait_for_job(
        job.get_id().unwrap(),
        std::time::Duration::from_secs(3),
        std::time::Duration::from_secs(300),
    ).await?;
    println!("Status: {:?}", result.status);

    Ok(())
}
```

## CLI Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `auth` | Manage API credentials |
| `me` | Show user info and credit balance |
| `models` | List available models |
| `styles` | List available image styles |
| `jobs` | Create and monitor jobs |
| `animate` | Animate a still image into video |
| `media` | Upload, download, and process media |
| `api-keys` | Manage API keys |

title: Rust4All Template
excerpt: A production-ready full-stack webapp template using Rust (Axum) + React (TypeScript). Clone, run, build — no API keys or configuration needed.
body_md:
# Rust4All Template

The full-stack Rust webapp template that just works. **Clone. Run. Build.** No API keys, no configuration, no headaches.

## 30-Second Start

```bash
git clone git@github.com:rust4ai/rust4all-template.git my-app
cd my-app
cp .env.example .env
./dev.sh
```

`dev.sh` handles everything: starts PostgreSQL (Docker), the Rust backend, and the React dev server.

## Stack

| Layer | Tech |
|-------|------|
| **API** | Axum 0.8 + Tokio |
| **Database** | PostgreSQL + SQLx |
| **Auth** | Google OAuth / dev login + JWT |
| **Frontend** | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 8 |
| **Styling** | Tailwind CSS 4 |
| **State** | Zustand |
| **Deploy** | Docker + Railway |

## Key Features

- **Zero-config development** — boots with an empty `.env`, dev-mode email login included
- **Production auth** — Google OAuth with JWT, ready for real users
- **One Docker image** — multi-stage build, deploy anywhere
- **Compile-time checked SQL** — SQLx ensures your queries are correct at build time
- **In-app docs** — markdown documentation served from a `/docs` route

title: Spice
excerpt: A Rust test framework for nondeterministic LLM agents — validate tool calls, arguments, security boundaries, and more with built-in retry and consensus.
body_md:
# Spice

A Rust test framework for nondeterministic LLM agents. Spice lets you write declarative test suites that validate your AI agent's behavior — which tools it calls, what arguments it passes, what text it produces, and whether it stays within security boundaries.

## Key Features

- **Fluent test builder** — chain assertions like `.expect_tools()`, `.expect_text_contains()`, `.forbid_tools()`
- **30+ built-in assertions** — tool usage, argument validation, call counts, ordering, turn ranges, security allowlists, and custom closures
- **Retry & consensus** — retry flaky tests N times, or require M-of-N runs to pass
- **Concurrent runner** — run tests in parallel with configurable concurrency
- **Trace recording** — every agent run is saved as JSON for debugging
- **Security assertions** — verify agents only call allowed tools, even under adversarial prompts
- **Multi-turn support** — assert tool usage across specific turns
- **Bring your own agent** — implement one trait (`AgentUnderTest`) to test any agent, any LLM provider

## Quick Start

```rust
use spice_framework::*;
use serde_json::json;

let suite = suite("My Agent Tests", vec![
    test("calls-tool", "Do the thing")
        .name("Should call myTool")
        .expect_tools(&["myTool"])
        .expect_tool_args_contain("myTool", json!({"key": "value"}))
        .retries(2)
        .build(),

    test("no-tools-on-greeting", "Hello!")
        .name("Greeting should not trigger tools")
        .expect_no_tools()
        .build(),
]);
```

title: Solarabase
excerpt: An agentic knowledgebase platform built in Rust — upload documents, auto-index them with an LLM-powered hierarchical tree index, and query them through an AI agent with per-KB API keys.
body_md:
# Solarabase

Solarabase is an **agentic knowledgebase platform** built entirely in Rust. Upload your documents, let Solarabase auto-index them with a **PageIndex** hierarchical tree index (LLM-generated), and query the result through an AI agent that can browse, search, and read your knowledge — all behind per-knowledgebase API keys.

It's Knowledgebase-as-a-Service: multi-tenant, billable, and ready to plug into your own agents via a clean retrieve API.

## Why Solarabase?

Most RAG stacks bolt a vector database onto a chunker and hope cosine similarity finds the right passage. Solarabase takes a different approach: every document is turned into an **LLM-generated tree index** — a hierarchical map of what the document contains, page by page — and the query agent *navigates* that tree with tools instead of relying on embedding similarity alone.

| | Solarabase | Typical RAG |
|---|---|---|
| **Indexing** | LLM-built hierarchical tree (PageIndex) | Fixed-size chunk + embed |
| **Retrieval** | Agent navigates tree with tools | Top-k vector similarity |
| **Backend** | Native Rust (Axum + SQLx) | Python services |
| **Multi-tenancy** | Workspace → KB → Docs, scoped by `kb_id` | Often single-tenant |
| **Integration** | Per-KB API keys + `/retrieve` endpoint | Custom glue |

## Key Features

- **Agentic retrieval** — A per-KB RAG agent answers questions using tools (`list_docs`, `search_index`, `read_page`) rather than blind similarity search
- **PageIndex hierarchical indexing** — A background worker builds a per-page tree index plus a root document index for every uploaded document
- **Multi-tenant by design** — Workspace → Knowledgebase → Documents, with every query scoped by `kb_id`
- **Per-KB API keys** — `sb_live_*` keys scoped to a single knowledgebase, SHA-256 hashed and shown once
- **Retrieve endpoint** — `/api/kb/:id/retrieve` returns RAG context *without* LLM synthesis, so you can wire Solarabase into your own external agents
- **Configurable models** — OpenAI by default (`gpt-4o`), configurable per knowledgebase
- **Stripe billing** — Free / Pro / Team plans with usage limits enforced at the API layer
- **Google OAuth** — JWT httpOnly cookie auth out of the box

## Stack

| Layer | Tech |
|-------|------|
| **Backend** | Rust + Axum + SQLx |
| **Frontend** | React + Vite + Tailwind CSS |
| **Database** | PostgreSQL (Neon) |
| **Storage** | S3-compatible (DigitalOcean Spaces) |
| **LLM** | OpenAI (`gpt-4o` default, per-KB configurable) |
| **Auth** | Google OAuth → JWT |
| **Billing** | Stripe |

## Architecture

```
User → Google OAuth → JWT Cookie → Axum API
                                      |
                              KbAccess extractor
                          (workspace membership OR API key)
                                      |
                              Per-KB RagAgent (cached)
                                   |      |
                            PageIndex    LLM Query
                            (indexer)    (tools: list_docs, search_index, read_page)
```

- **Indexer** — A background worker processes all pending documents globally, building per-page tree indexes and a root document index via the LLM.
- **RagCache** — An LRU cache of `Arc<RagAgent>` per knowledgebase, evicted after 30 minutes idle.
- **Retrieve** — `/api/kb/:id/retrieve` exposes pure RAG context for integrating Solarabase into external agent pipelines.

## Use It From Your Own Agent

Because every knowledgebase has a scoped API key and a synthesis-free retrieve endpoint, Solarabase drops cleanly into an existing agent stack:

```bash
curl -X POST https://your-solarabase/api/kb/$KB_ID/retrieve \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sb_live_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "What is our refund policy?"}'
```

You get back the most relevant pages from the tree index — feed them straight into your own LLM prompt, or let Solarabase's built-in agent synthesize the answer for you.

## Resources

- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/rust4ai/solarabase-monorepo)
